revision_summary: Two minor wrong_ts quote issues need correction: (1) multi_touch_patterns[0].touches[1] at claimed ts 04:32 — the full quote spans 04:32 through 05:03 ('...if you guys subtract or something... a heavy rain or snow, and then came up the problem... Who is it going to cover?'); Stage 3 should either use the correct span or pick the ts where 'Who is it going to cover?' actually lands (05:03). (2) multi_touch_patterns[1].touches[1] at claimed ts 06:35 — this is a composite of two customer lines 25 seconds apart (06:35-06:40 and 06:59-07:11) with rep dialogue between them; Stage 3 should split this into two touches or clearly mark it as a paraphrased composite rather than a single contiguous quote. Additionally: (a) reconsider bill_anchor_audit's 'bill_captured: true' — the $200 figure is the customer's own rough guess, not an actual bill capture, and the call explicitly defers real bill collection to a callback; this should be marked as a soft/estimated capture, not a full capture, to avoid misleading downstream aggregation. (b) Fix the schema_reference in cherry_pick_moments[2] (06:12) — cross_sell_signals.roof_replacement_planned is the wrong key for net-metering/backyard-panel interest; cite analysis_directives.cross_sell_signal_detection or flag as an uncatalogued cross-sell signal instead. (c) Add two missed moments to cherry_pick_moments: the unresolved referral request at 07:12 ('would you be able to refer me some other company?') which the rep never answers or logs into the handoff_brief promises, and the tech-friction moment at 11:47 (customer can't access online utility account) as a root-cause contributor to the soft-exit outcome, per tech_friction_handling directive. (d) Note the inconsistent treatment of transcript garbling — Stage 3 flags transcription ambiguity as a mitigating factor at 09:40 but not at 08:04, despite similar overlapping/garbled speech in both; apply the same caveat consistently or justify why one moment is treated as clean evidence and the other isn't. All other quotes, the strategic-vs-reactive calls, the trajectory verdict, and the outcome dispute are well-supported and should be retained as-is.
